newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says to buy 110,000 T rice at Oct 24 tender.
newsitem.headline: Japan says to buy 110,000 T rice at Oct 24 tender.

text.p: The Japanese Food Agency said on Monday that it would buy 110,000 tonnes of rice at its import tender on October 24.
The agency also said it would buy 10,000 tonnes of rice at its November 8 tender.

Under a 1993 General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade agreement, Japan agreed to gradually open its long-closed rice market and committed itself to importing 511,000 tonnes of rice during the year to the end of next March.

But so far this fiscal year, the Food Agency, the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry and the sole importer of rice, has bought only 39,500 tonnes, mainly from China and Australia. It bought the rice at the last tender in late July.

The rice import tender was delayed because of ample stocks and the general election on Sunday, industry officials said. Some rice exporters, particularly Australia, have expressed frustration at the delay.
"We're going to carry out another tenders later this year to finish rice import for this fiscal year," a Food Agency official said.
